card.name: Dosing schedule and dose-change wording
card.fires_on: Words in dosing instructions that precede a schedule or dose term, such as 'alternate day', 'in the morning', 'gradually reduce', 'immunosuppressive doses'. Also seen partway through a drug name or 'first trimester'.

modes.label: Schedule words
modes.description: Time-of-day or alternate-day wording in how to give a drug.
modes.example: cyclophosphamide for injection should be administered in the<< morning>>. 2.2 Recommended Dosage

modes.label: Dose change verbs
modes.description: Verbs about lowering or continuing a dose, just before 'the dosage'.
modes.example: Gradually<< reduce>> the dosage rather than stopping Paroxetine H

modes.label: Partway through terms
modes.description: Inside a brand name or the word trimester.
modes.example: first<< trimest>>er paroxetine use in pregnancy and congen

card.writes: It pushes toward dose and amount words and away from words like produced or products.
card.plain: It lights up on wording about when to give a drug or how to taper the dose.
